top_signals.title: UK Inflation Set to Rebound as Energy Bills Surge
top_signals.summary: Rising energy prices are poised to send UK inflation rearing back up, as economists warn that the summer boost to the economy could be fleeting. The rate of Consumer Prices Index (CPI) inflation is tipped to rise to 2.9 per cent in July, climbing from June’s 15-month low of 2.6 per cent, when the Office for National Statistics (ONS) releases its figures on Wednesday. While frequent heatwaves and the World Cup have boosted the UK’s summer economy, economists are sounding the alarm over Ofgem’s recent hike to its energy price cap.…
top_signals.why_it_matters: Inflation expectations impacting rate path, bonds and global risk assets.

top_signals.title: Cheap Drones, Dry Taps: The Iran War Opens a New Era of Water Infrastructure Risk
top_signals.summary:

top_signals.title: AstraZeneca Reports Mixed Lung Cancer Trial Results
top_signals.summary: AstraZeneca is stopping a clinical trial of the experimental drug volrustomig as it didn’t look set to help fight lung cancer better than existing therapies. The company had two separate late-stage trial successes that strengthen key cancer franchises, including one where patients with non-small cell lung cancer received Tagrisso in combination with Orpathys. Bloomberg Intelligence's Sam Fazeli has more on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: Blanchard’s Lathe and the Long Arc of American Manufacturing
top_signals.summary:
Emerging from the chaos of supplying the U.S. Army during the War of 1812, the War Department sought to foster domestic production of standardized muskets. Out of this industrial project arose an invention that laid the foundation for automation and mass production. Thomas Blanchard’s copying lathe was a product of a fluid interchange between public and private interests, expertise, and capital. Born into the mechanical milieu of the nineteenth-century Connecticut River Valley, Blanchard embodied the period’s spirit of ingenuity.
